title: fix(post): the Tormach safe retract comes from the machine file
body:
## What changed

The Tormach post's safe retract `G53 G0 Z0` assumed machine Z0 is the top of Z travel. That holds on a Tormach, but on a LinuxCNC machine homed with Z0 at the bottom it rapids down into the part (reported on #435).

- **Machine file:** an optional `safe_retract` on the linear Z part gives the retract Z in MACHINE coordinates, in the file's length unit (scaled like travel). Zero counts as a stated value. A non-number, or the key on any other axis, refuses the file and names the axis. The mirror carries it as `safeRetractZ` (mm). The script sees `machine.safeRetractZ` (or `null`) and `machine.model`, the model name through either door (app mirror or CLI raw file).
- **Shipped machines:** every Tormach `.mch` states `0.0`. So do `vmc.mch`, `tilthead.mch` and the default `3axis-vmc.mch` (`"safeRetractZ": 0.0`).
- **tormach.cps:**
  - A stated safe Z posts `G53 G0 Z<that>`.
  - With no machine, or a model named "Tormach..." that states no safe Z, the output is unchanged (`G53 G0 Z0` + `G30`).
  - Any other machine that states no safe Z gets one counted `message()` that names the machine and the key, and no retract line is written. The in-app gate blocks the write.
  - A non-zero safe Z drops `G30`, because an unset G30 position on LinuxCNC is the machine origin. The header then says `(SAFE RETRACT G53 Z<v> - STATED BY THE MACHINE)`.
- **Docs:** `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/495-safe-retract.md` (alternatives considered, plus notes on the other posts).

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_safe_retract.rs`:
- `the_shipped_tormach_machines_post_byte_identical`: every library Tormach posts byte-identical with and without the key. A null machine and the default VMC also keep `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30`.
- `a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: covers the mirror and the raw door. An inch file scales, there is no G30, and the header comment is written.
- `a_non_tormach_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`: covers the mirror and the raw door, and checks that a Tormach-named file without the key still posts Z0.
- `a_garbled_safe_retract_refuses_the_file`

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all), plus 64 camcraft-app suites touching posts and machines, all green. These include conformance (every golden byte-exact), tormach_post, tormach_machines, machine, machine_library, posting, fanuc_post, inverted_post, program_comments, project_roundtrip, wear_comp and control_comp. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real machine cut and no Hub sim.
- The UI machine sheet does not show the new key yet.
- The CLI `post` binary was not smoke-run by hand. Its raw-door path is covered by the tests.
- Behaviour change: a document saved before this change with a mounted non-Tormach machine (for example the library "VMC 3-axis") stores that machine without the key. Posting it through the Tormach post is now refused by name until the machine is re-mounted.

Changelog: Tormach post retracts to the machine's stated safe Z (`safe_retract`, machine coordinates) and refuses a non-Tormach machine that states none, instead of assuming machine Z0 is the top of travel

Fixes #495

title: feat(post): probe positioning moves post as protected stop-on-contact moves
body:
## What changed

The positioning feeds of a probe cycle (the descent from the rapid / safe plane to each touch's start, the bore entry to its centre, the rise back to the safe plane) were plain G01. They now post as protected moves: stop on contact and alarm if the stylus trips on the way.

- **Stream:** `post::dump` marks every non-rapid straight move of a path that carries probing touches, other than the touches and their incremental back-offs, as a new `GUARD x y z F feed` record (`Record::Guard`, `probe_rec::GuardRec`, documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`). An arc or a feed with no rate in a probe path is refused with a WARN. The safe-plane rapids stay rapids.
- **Engine:** the new `onProbeGuard` hook (properties `X Y Z Feed`, `StartX/Y/Z`). A script without it is refused by name, once per operation. There is no PRELUDE default, because a plain feed would be the silent wrong answer.
- **Fanuc (`fanuc.cps`):** `G31 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then for each moving axis `IF[ABS[#506n-<end>]GT0.001]THEN#3000=3(PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)`. This works because, with no skip signal, the skip position is the block end.
- **Tormach PathPilot (`tormach.cps`):** `G38.3 X.. Y.. Z.. F..`, then `oN if [#5070 EQ 1]` / `(MSG, PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING)` / `M2` / `oN endif`, with O-words from 5001.
- **Inverted axes (`invert.rs`):** a GUARD is mirrored like an absolute move.
- **Viewer map (`posting.rs`):** a GUARD counts as one motion record.

Sources (behaviour only): Fanuc's published custom macro B / G31 skip documentation (#5061-#5063, #3000); the LinuxCNC G-code reference (G38.3, #5070, O-code conditionals, MSG); Tormach's PathPilot machine-code reference (G38.2-G38.5 and M2 supported).

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/probe_guard.rs`:
  - `the_positioning_feeds_of_a_probe_path_are_marked_protected`: every mode; no plain feed left; GUARD count per mode; one record per move.
  - `the_guard_record_round_trips_and_refuses_malformed_lines`
  - `fanuc_writes_protected_moves_as_g31_with_a_contact_alarm`: new golden `nc/fanuc/probe_corner.nc`.
  - `tormach_writes_protected_moves_as_g38_3_with_a_trip_test`: new golden `nc/tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`. It pins the guard blocks only, because Tormach's touches are #362 / PR #376.
  - `a_probing_post_without_on_probe_guard_is_refused_by_name`
- Regenerated Fanuc goldens: `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_corner_negative`, `probe_edge_negative_x`. The only change is G01 → G31 + the alarm line.
- `probe_op::the_posted_g31_z_is_the_tip_at_the_expected_contact` now tells touches from guards.
- Gate: these camcraft-app binaries are green, all run on the final head: conformance, fanuc_post, inverted_axis_display, inverted_equivalence, inverted_post, per_op_files, post_not_judged, posting, probe_guard, probe_op, probe_pick, probe_reach, project_roundtrip, scripting, tormach_machines, tormach_post. All camcraft-post tests are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No real controller or PathPilot Hub run. The G38.3 / #5070 block and the Fanuc G31 alarm are checked against the documentation only.
- Tormach probe-op end to end: Tormach has no `onProbeMove` on main, so this waits for #376.

## Overlaps

- **#376 (Tormach G38.2):** my Tormach hook sits in its own section, away from #376's hunks. Its probe goldens will gain the G38.3 blocks.
- **#360 (Haas / Mazak / Siemens):** those scripts need `onProbeGuard`, or their probe ops are refused by name once this merges.
- **#465 (inverted probing):** `invert.rs` gets a separate Guard arm that mirrors without refusing, so it is covered by #465's translation.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/174-probe-protected-descent.md`.

Changelog: Probe op positioning moves (descent, bore entry, rise) post as protected stop-on-contact moves that alarm on an unexpected trip: G31 + #3000 on Fanuc, G38.3 + #5070 on Tormach PathPilot; a probing post without `onProbeGuard` is refused by name.

Fixes #174

title: test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 2 of #339, answered by tests rather than new law. The full analysis is posted on #339.

## What this is
Slice 2 asked whether the mesh law must also **convict**: catch penetrations the box laws let through.

**Answer: no.**
- A meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the same transformed vertices the mesh law reads (`model::entity_world_aabb` / `world_facets`). `mesh_refined` only reads a mesh whose AABB equals the law's box, and non-finite meshes keep the box verdict. So the mesh always sits inside its box, rotated fixtures and overhangs included.
- Every deliberate silence of the box laws allows an overlap of at most `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1e-9) with the box. That covers the strict z overlap in `band_hits_box` (c2, plus #464's d2 upper bands and flute column) and the strict-dip rule in `rapid_hits_box`. An overlap that small with the box can't be more than that with the mesh.
- Everything else is an enclosure, not a silence.

## What changed
New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs` (5 tests, with a gate-map header). Each composes the box laws with `mesh_refined` the way `posting::fixture_problems` does.
- **A mesh top face keeps the strict dip:** a retract off it, a traverse riding it and a cut riding it are silent. The same moves 0.001 lower report Rapid and Flute.
- **A rotated fixture's top edge is its box's top:** a block turned 45° about X, then 30° about Z.
- **An overhanging arm convicts the stack under it:** the Shank under the arm and the Holder rim off its end both hit. Its top stays flush-silent.
- **The #424 and #425 repros convict on a closed mesh** (Holder), from the box law and the mesh alike.
- **No straight move the box laws clear penetrates the mesh:** a seeded sweep of 12,000 moves biased onto flush planes. 7,045 are silent (103 in flush contact), and none penetrates the mesh. Lowering the box top 0.01 mm makes this test fail at once, which shows it catches real gaps.

## Found along the way (filed separately)
**#491:** the box laws judge an XY arc by its **inscribed** chords at the bare band radius, so steel within the arc's sagitta (about 0.01 mm on R30) is missed. This applies to every fixture, not only meshed ones, so the fix belongs in the box law. It is out of this slice's scope.

## How tested
- `fixture_mesh_convict` 5/5, `fixture_mesh` 9 passed (1 ignored), `fixture_stack_span` 8/8.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- Test-only: no product code changes.

Changelog: none (test-only)

Refs #339

title: feat(sim): judge posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves against the fixture mesh
body:
**Stacked on #476** (#339 slice 1, fixture mesh). Slice 3 of #339 per the triage on the issue: posed, rotary and XZ/YZ-arc moves read against the fixture mesh. Slice 1 left those on the box verdict. As before, **the mesh only ever clears a hit the box law flagged; it never adds one.**

## What changed
**Frames.**
- **Path frame:** steel that turns with the part, and any steel when no rotary axis is stated (the box laws' frame).
- **Machine frame, A rotary:** fixed steel under an A rotary op, carried per stretch by `posed_steel::upright_turn`, the same frame `workholding` uses. A pose the rotary alone can't stand upright keeps the box verdict.
- **Machine frame, spindle C:** each move's C line is recovered from its two stated C angles. Fixed steel gets one exact sweep of the machine's straight station run. Steel turning with the part is read along the real spiral, in stretches turned by −C.
- **XZ/YZ arcs:** chorded in their own plane, with the same sagitta pad as XY arcs.
- **Left to the box:**
  - a C move whose start C isn't the previous move's;
  - a non-horizontal C pose;
  - a C turn under 1e-4 rad or near 180°;
  - a held C under fixed steel;
  - fixed steel under both a rotary axis and C;
  - an arc on a C move.

**Why a "clear" is safe.**
1. Each posed move is split into stretches by its pose turn (`midpose::turn_intervals`). Over a stretch the tip stays on its segment within the chord pad, and the pose stays within `swing` of the stretch axis, by midpose's existing rate bound.
2. A band point `p(t) + Q(t)y` stays within `swing·hypot(max(|lo|,|hi|), r)` of the unturned band. So the band lies inside segment ⊕ oriented cylinder ⊕ ball(pad), a convex set.
3. GJK sweeps the segment and cylinder exactly, and the ball goes into the margin. "Clear" is returned only with a separating-plane proof. A non-finite input or NaN margin counts as a hit.
4. A turn into another frame adds `dth·ρmax`, with ρmax taken at the stretch's four parallelogram corners plus r + pad. Distance to a line is convex, so that bounds it.
5. Consecutive stretches overlap at their shared instant, so one inside-the-solid point per band decides. Using an oriented cylinder rather than a capsule means a tilted tool isn't falsely convicted on a vise floor below its tip.

**Labels.** A mesh-kept rapid hit names a band above the flute by its part (Shank, Holder, Spindle), like #464's law (d2). This now applies on the posed and C paths too.

`docs/decisions/339-mesh-posed.md`, including a finding filed as **#486**: `cl::stamp_c` pieces keep the whole move's tool axis, so the box laws may misjudge fixed steel on C turns. The mesh can't fix that, since it only clears hits.

## How tested
- **New sim `fixture_mesh_posed`** (9 tests, plus 1 heavy-lane):
  - a tilted pass, an in-place index and a tilted rapid down a vise gap are cleared, while the same index into a jaw and a rapid swung into the other jaw still convict;
  - A-rotary fixed and turning steel, each with a clear case and a convicting case;
  - C turns with turning and fixed steel; a move with no prior C, and an axial tool, keep the box verdict;
  - XZ arcs, one clear and one dipping 0.21 mm into the base; a YZ arc in the gap is clear;
  - a posed rapid kept by the mesh names its band;
  - both turn signs (A and C) pinned by mutation.
- **New app `fixture_mesh_posed`** (2 tests): a 3+2 face indexed B 10° between closed jaws. The box law alone convicts every move, yet the post and generation are clean. With the jaws 1 mm into reach, the post is blocked and generation warns.
- **One slice-1 pin renamed** (`unpaired_boxes_keep_the_box_verdict_and_posed_moves_are_read`): a posed gap pass is now cleared.
- **Existing suites keep their verdicts:** posed_fixture, posed_fixture_midpose, posed_rapids, midmove_pose, fixture_stack_span, sim lib; app fixtures, rotary_fixtures, fixture_mesh, fixture_law_gaps. Their fixtures are box-only or open, so the mesh never judges them.
- **Performance:**
  - debug, 29.7k facets and 80 posed moves: 0.07 s;
  - release heavy lane, 203k facets and 2000 posed moves: 0.33 s.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
No GUI or G-code change. More 4/5-axis and rotary programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions on tilted, rotary and spindle-C moves and XZ/YZ arcs are judged against the fixture's real mesh too, so a tilted pass between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

Refs #339

title: feat(mcp): render_stock - the simulated stock as a PNG image block
body:
**Replaces #364**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #364 can no longer be updated. This branch carries the merge with main at #461. The conflicts were the MCP module/import lists (#180's pick/area/features and this PR's render), all kept. After the merge: `mcp_render` 5/5, `mcp` 9/9, clippy clean.

## What changed
- **New MCP tool `render_stock`.** It runs the post gate's own program simulation (`stock_sim::simulate_document`) and paints what stands by deviation class: clean, rest, gouge, unjudged.
  - **CPU rasteriser.** It draws the result with a new rasteriser (`crates/app/src/raster.rs`): flat-shaded triangles through a depth buffer, orthographic camera, PNG via the `png` crate. No GPU.
  - **Answer.** The PNG comes back as an MCP image content block (`{"type":"image","data":…,"mimeType":"image/png"}`) after the text block. Alongside it, a JSON summary gives:
    - rest and gouge cell counts, volume, maximum and where it is;
    - the rest's top bounds and the drawn stock's bounds;
    - judged-cell count and image facts.
  - **Arguments:** `width`/`height` (16–2048, default 640×480), `view` (`iso` | `top`), `toolpath` (bool: feed, plunge and rapid moves drawn over the stock).
  - **Refusals, each named:** no simulation (no stock or nothing generated), no material standing above the stock floor, bad or unknown arguments. Unsupported programs (5-axis, rotary, lathe) refuse with the sim's own reason, as the post gate does.
- `mcp/mod.rs` `tool_ok` lifts the PNG out of the JSON into the image block, so neither the text nor `structuredContent` carries the base64.
- `mcp/tools.rs` gets one table row only. **Note:** PR #314 also adds a row to this table, so a one-line conflict is possible and trivial to resolve.
- **Dependency:** `png = "0.18"` is now a direct dependency of `camcraft-app`, declared in the workspace. It was already in `Cargo.lock` through `image`, so no new crate enters the tree (MIT/Apache-2.0). base64 is hand-written (a few lines) rather than a new crate.
- `docs/decisions/182-mcp-sim-render.md`

## How tested
- New `crates/app/tests/mcp_render.rs` (5 tests):
  - Uncut job: the PNG decodes at the requested size, stock covers the frame, rest volume is 8000 (40×40×5), and the base64 is not in the JSON.
  - The same session gives the same bytes twice, and a fresh session gives the same bytes too.
  - The top view with the toolpath overlay contains the feed-move colour.
  - `render_stock_shows_what_the_program_cut`: Face 2 mm down changes the bytes, the stock top goes to z 18 and rest to 4800. Facing down to the part top takes rest to 0 and removes every amber pixel (more than 10% of the frame repaints).
  - `render_stock_refuses_when_no_material_stands`: facing below the stock floor refuses by name, where it used to draw a flat sheet under the block.
  - The tool is listed with its schema, and every argument refusal is named.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_render --test mcp`: 9 passed. `clippy -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main` fell back to batch because Cargo.toml changed. The only failures also fail on `upstream/main` c442118 on this machine:
  - `probe_op::every_older_kind_keeps_its_stored_id_and_digest_tag` (version pin; PR #345)
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` ×2 (PR #351)
  - the headless-GPU ui tests (no adapter here)
  - the two macOS pixel-snapshot diffs (#255 / PR #359)

## Not exercised
- Not tried from a real MCP client (Claude Desktop etc.). Only the JSON-RPC tool path is tested.

Changelog: MCP `render_stock` returns a PNG of the simulated stock (by deviation class, optional toolpath overlay) with rest and gouge volume and bounds (#182)

Fixes #182

title: feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh
body:
**Replaces #430**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so it can no longer be updated. This branch carries the merges with main through #461: the mesh law reads #381's `HolderStack` (`steel_stack(geom, holder, spindle)`, with `mesh_refined` wrapping the `*_held` laws), and #395's turning holder judge is kept. The recipe in the old 'merge note for #381' below is now done.

Slice 1 of #339 (triage and split are on the issue). Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh, so a path down a vise's gap posts clean.

## What changed
**The box laws still run first, and the mesh can only clear a hit.** When a fixture's world box flags an upright move (laws c2 and d2), the fixture's closed mesh gets the final say, and it can only clear that hit, never add one. That keeps the box laws' deliberate silences, such as a retract off the mounting face. Where nothing is cleared, output is identical to before, labels included.

**Test shape.** Each tool band (flute, shank, holder, and the spindle housing when stated) is an upright cylinder swept along the move, an exact convex shape. Arcs are split into chords, each padded by how far the true arc can stray from it, plus 1 µm.

**Why it can't miss a real hit:**
- A band counts as clear only when a GJK distance test proves a gap of more than `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (plus the arc pad) to every nearby triangle. If the search fails or runs out, the answer is a hit.
- A band far from every triangle could still be buried inside the solid, so a point of it is tested by ray parity. Six fixed off-axis rays are tried; any that graze an edge, vertex or face are discarded, and if all are ambiguous the point counts as inside.
- Only closed meshes judge (each edge used once in each direction).
- A bounding-volume tree over the triangles is pruned with the same proof at every node.

**What keeps the box verdict:**
- Meshes that are open, non-finite, fully collapsed or over 4M facets: a named `MeshError`, logged.
- Tilted moves, moves with a non-zero C angle, and XZ/YZ arcs.
- Lathe tool kinds and non-mill machines.
- A box shared by two fixtures.

**Performance (release):**
- A 203k-facet closed mesh: validate and build the tree in 0.05 s.
- Worst case, 2000 passes grazing it 0.05 mm off (every one inside its box): 0.74 s total (0.37 ms/move), all correctly cleared.

**Code:**
- New: `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/` (mod, gjk, bvh, ray), `crates/sim/src/verify/mesh_steel.rs`.
- Hooks: `fixture::meshes_for`, plus small edits in `operation/{job,generate}.rs` and `posting.rs` (meshes cached once per setup).
- `docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md`

**Merge note for #381:** this edits next to #381's `HolderStack` changes in `posting.rs` `fixture_problems` and `generate.rs` `workholding_warnings`. Whichever lands second resolves by keeping `mesh_refined(path, &wh, &steel, rapids, |w| <law>)` with the closures calling #381's `_held` variants, and by building `steel_stack` from the `HolderStack` bands. The decisions file has the recipe.

## How tested
- `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (8 tests, plus one in the heavy lane):
  - a vise-gap pass, plunge and arc are cleared;
  - a jaw-corner clip still hits, while the same line 4.95 mm off is cleared;
  - a jaw-face clip, a holder over a jaw, a rapid into a jaw top, and a tool buried in steel all still hit;
  - open, NaN, empty and collapsed meshes refuse by name and keep the box verdict;
  - a tilted move and a fixture-less table box keep the box verdict;
  - timings (heavy lane: the 200k-facet case).
- `crates/app/tests/fixture_mesh.rs` (3 tests), end to end through `posting::verification_gate` and regeneration:
  - vise jaws 3 mm off the pass: clean;
  - the same vise as an open sheet: box verdict;
  - jaws 1 mm into the pass: the post is blocked and generation warns.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick upstream/main`: sim suites green; app suites green except `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…`, which is red on plain main (#415). Every existing fixture suite is unchanged.
- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised / follow-ups
- **Two P0 gaps in the existing box laws** were found by this survey and filed separately: #424 (upright rapids check only the flute) and #425 (ramps judged at their lowest z). This slice does not fix them, since the mesh only clears hits. The triage's slice 2 makes the mesh law able to add hits too.
- The remaining #339 slices: tilted and rotary moves against the mesh, fixture UX, routing around fixtures, and a fixture library.
- No GUI change, and no change to posted G-code. More programs now post: those whose only "hit" was a box around empty space between jaws.

Changelog: Fixture collisions are judged against the fixture's real mesh (the box stays the broad phase), so a path between vise jaws no longer refuses the post (#339)

Refs #339

title: feat(ui): import, place and draw a tool's holder body in the tool editor and sim
body:
**Replaces #399**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so it can no longer be updated. This branch carries the merges with main through #461, including #381, #395 and #431, and #348's tool-library commits, since #348 was closed unmerged.

**Stacked on #381** (tool bodies: `SetToolBody`, the envelope) **and #348** (tool library buttons in the same editor page). This diff includes both until they merge; the #371 work is e0219f1. Part of #361.

## What changed
**Tool editor: a "Tool body" column.**
- **Import body…** (STEP/STL/OBJ through the app's importer) and **Clear body**.
- Placement controls: an axis combo (±X/±Y/±Z of the model, or a picked direction), **Tip offset**, and **Pick tip** / **Pick axis** toggles.
- A small 3D preview: egui-painted, drag to orbit, no GPU.
- A live placement note ("placed: foot … to top …" or the reason it won't place), and **Apply body**.
- The 2D profile preview draws the placed body's revolved envelope in amber over the cylinders.
- A tool not yet in the document shows "Add the tool first…".

**Picking.** A click casts a ray through `tool_body_view::pick`.
- **Pick tip** snaps to the nearest corner of the hit facet and sets the offset so that corner is the tip.
- **Pick axis** takes the clicked facet's outward normal.
- Picks only fill the fields; they never queue a command.

**Commands.**
- **Apply body** queues one `SetToolBody`, a single undo step. **Clear body** is the same command with `None`.
- Refusals show in the editor by name ("tool body not set: …", "tool body not imported: …") and the draft is kept.
- The draft reloads only when the world's body changes (Apply / Undo / Redo / Open), so an unapplied import survives other edits.

**Simulation.** While the transport runs, the running tool's body is posed at the playhead (read from the cached timeline) and drawn as a shaded, depth-tested part. A tool without a body draws exactly as before.

**App-layer helpers**, so ui stays thin: `crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs` holds `load`, `preview` (the same place-and-envelope step as the command, uncommitted), `pick`, `tip_offset_at`, `posed` and `body_for_operation`.

`docs/decisions/371-tool-body-ui.md` records why picking lives in the editor's own preview rather than the main viewport. Among other reasons, a pick mode there would compete with the face/edge/vertex picks.

## How tested
- New app `tool_body_view` (6 tests). `tool_body` (8) still passes.
- 6 new structural UI tests (`egui_app/tests/tool_body.rs`):
  - the editor offers Import/Clear;
  - Apply lands one `SetToolBody`, with Undo/Redo and Clear plus its undo;
  - a degenerate placement is refused by name;
  - a tip pick fills the offset and queues nothing;
  - a missing file is refused by name;
  - the sim draws the body at the playhead, and nothing without one.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 307 passed. `--test operations`: 31/31. `clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings`: clean.
- **Expected failure: the pixel snapshot `tool_editor_snapshot`.** The editor is wider (third column) and anchored further left, so its pixels changed. The PNG is deliberately **not** regenerated: #359 (#255) moves pixel goldens to the release lane, after which this test runs and is refreshed only at the cut. The headless-GPU tests also fail here (no adapter on this Mac), the same as on main.

## Not exercised (draft until the contributor tries a build)
- Hands-on GUI check: the import, picking, apply/undo and simulation flow, on a release build.
- The body file is read on the UI thread, so a very large vendor STEP freezes the window briefly while loading.
- Not in this slice: lathe-body placement UI (#369's frame), turning the body about its axis for display, and drawing a body outside the simulation.

Changelog: The tool editor imports a holder body (STEP/STL/OBJ), places it by picking its tip and axis, and the simulation draws the real holder (#371)

Fixes #371

title: fix(post): judge the tool-number clash per machine
body:
**Replaces #440**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #440 can no longer be updated. **Now stacked on #471** (the replacement for #439).

(Originally stacked on #439.) The #438 work is 9d9ac93d.

## What changed
- **The tool-number clash check (#221) is judged per machine.** `tool_numbers::clash_per_machine` runs the existing `clash()` on each machine group from `program_mounts(world, false)`. `posting::op_streams` calls it, which covers per-op files too.
- **Why per machine, not per NC file:** a T number names a pocket in one machine's tool changer.
  - Two machines have two tool tables, so T2 on each is fine.
  - Two posts on one machine still load from one carousel, so a shared number there is still refused.
  - Grouping per file (machine plus post) would let that real clash through, so I rejected it.
- **Messages:** a single-machine program gets the exact #221 message, unchanged. A multi-machine refusal starts with the mount's label (`Setup1 (machine, post): tools '…' and '…' would both post as T3 …`).
- The rationale is in `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` (#438 section).

## How tested
- New `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one`:
  - across machines: a mill tool numbered 2 and the lathe's T2 post as two files;
  - within one machine: a clash is refused, naming both tools, the T number and Setup1, and not the lathe tool.
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name` (single machine) is unchanged and passes.
- `setup_mounts_post` 6/6, `setup_mount` 6/6, `tool_numbers` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `post_not_judged` 4/4. `clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: The tool-number clash is judged per machine, so two machines in one program may each use the same T number (#438)

Fixes #438

title: feat(post): probing on an inverted X/Y axis for the Fanuc post
body:
Part of #372. Lifts the #374 refusal of probing on an inverted X/Y, for Fanuc. Haas follows when its probing hooks land (PR #360), hence `Refs #392`.

## What changed
- **Translation.** `post::invert` mirrors the probing records on an inverted X/Y, the same way it mirrors a move. It negates the TOUCH target and expected trip, the RETREAT back-off delta and its end point, and each FOUND axis's expected value.
- **New manifest flag `probeAxisInversion = true`.** The translation runs only for a post script that declares it, and only `fanuc.cps` does. Haas declares `axisInversion` but not this flag, so it refuses probing by name. Posts without `axisInversion` already refuse any inverted machine.

**Why negating is right.** The controller position is `M = G54 + P`, and the tip stands at `S·M`, where S = −1 on the inverted axis.
- The posted `P = S(W − origin)` lands correctly only if G54 holds `S·D`.
- A part off by d trips at `S(W_trip + d − origin)`. The translated expected value is `S(W_trip − origin)`, so the deviation is `S·d`.
- `G10 L2 X[#5221+dev]` then gives `S(D + d)`: the real part's datum in controller coordinates.
- Back-offs are increments, so they flip with the axis. `ABS[dev]` and the choice of travel axis are sign-free.
- In full: `docs/decisions/392-probe-inverted-axis.md`.

## How tested
New `inverted_probe` (8 tests). The posted Fanuc programs run on a **test-only macro-B controller** (`crates/app/tests/macro_b/`): G31 trips where the stylus first meets a simulated part, every G0/G1 is collision-checked, and unmodelled words are errors.
- **Physical offset:** face −Z, face −X, edge −Y, corners +X+Y and −X−Y, bore and boss, each on standard, inverted-X, inverted-Y and inverted-XY machines, with the part shifted (0.37, −0.21, −0.13) mm.
  - G55 always ends at the physical datum, within 0.002.
  - G54 is untouched, and unmeasured axes aren't written.
  - The standard machine gives the same answer, which checks the interpreter.
- **Edge cases:** a part exactly on the model returns the datum unchanged. No contact raises `#3000=2`, and out of tolerance raises `#3000=1`.
- **Converse checks:** the untranslated program misses on an inverted machine. Undoing any one translated word breaks it: a stylus crash, a tolerance alarm, or probing past overtravel.
- **Both sign forms:** the reader accepts the old `#100--2.5` and the folded `#100+2.5` from #386, which is now on main. Re-run after merging main: 8/8.
- **Existing suites:** `inverted_post`, `inverted_equivalence`, `axis_direction`, `probe_op`, `probe_reach`, `fanuc_post`, `conformance` and the camcraft-post suites pass. **No golden changed.** `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except #415, which is red on main.

## Not exercised
No run on a real control with an inverted axis. The macro interpreter proves the arithmetic and motion of the posted words.

Changelog: Probing posts on a Fanuc machine with an inverted X/Y axis (the probe records are mirrored like moves; the written work offset is the physical correction) (#392)

Refs #392
